trajectoryRevisions.name: T1 v2 · Thiên Kiếm
trajectoryRevisions.prompt:
Edit the attached 4-panel Wudang Sword game storyboard. Preserve its polished hand-pixelled chibi characters, costume, facing, one physical sword pointing toward the boss, stone surface, fixed elevated orthographic camera, 2-by-2 layout and exact numbers 1, 2, 3, 4. Preserve the ONE target mark centered at the same boss's feet in each panel. Make a substantial, unambiguous correction to the AIRBORNE SWORD FLIGHT. The path has a tall rounded inverted U shape, like a high fountain arch: nearly vertical climb, rounded high crest, near-vertical tip-down drop. Give the flight much more visible height than before. Keep the caster and boss anchored low in the composition and all airborne steel weapons fully inside the panels. Use small clear steel jian silhouettes with blades, guards and grips. There is no text besides the four existing numbers.

Panel 1, top left: same aim and marker. No airborne swords yet.
Panel 2, top right: this panel shows ONLY the first, nearly vertical ascent. All the flying swords have their TIPS pointing UP, parallel to the left/right edges. A tall, narrow vertical column of over a dozen distinct ascending steel swords stays DIRECTLY ABOVE the caster's rear shoulder and back at the left side of the panel. Several swords already reach more than two character heights over the caster. Their thin trailing motion streaks run straight up from the rear shoulder. The right-hand two-thirds of this panel remain entirely empty above the boss. This must read like an upward fountain launch, with no diagonal fan or sideways travel during this phase.
Panel 3, bottom left: the signature image. Show one CLEAR COMPLETE high rounded arch of trails from directly above the caster's back at the left, curling up steeply, cresting in the top-center with a horizontal tangent, then curving smoothly down above the boss on the right. It must clearly draw a tall ∩ silhouette, with a tall left leg, one rounded top, and a tall right leg. Leave the central space below the bridge of the arch open so the shape reads instantly. Distribute many small swords along the curve and turn their tips tangent to travel: UP on the left leg, RIGHT only at the rounded top, DOWN on the right leg. The drawing should read as an airborne trajectory, no closed portal ring, no tangled loops, no diagonal spray crossing the center.
Panel 4, bottom right: dramatic descent from directly OVER the boss. Only near-vertical downward-moving blades above the boss, with tips down and slender vertical trails behind them. Numerous blades funnel into the ONE unchanged mark under the boss, with a short low impact splash that preserves his silhouette. No sword hits by the caster and no broad diagonal delivery. Keep the style and contrast of the attached board, and keep every character and blade silhouette clean and legible.
Keep the original T1 spectral silver blades with small gold guards, restrained icy-blue and pale silver trails, and a crisp white-blue ground impact. Several slim companion trails can trace the same high arch in parallel so the high crest is clearly visible.

trajectoryRevisions.name: T1 v3 · Kiếm từ trời
trajectoryRevisions.prompt:
Edit this exact four-panel polished pixel-art gameplay storyboard for the Wudang ultimate Van Kiem Quy Tong. Preserve the original OPTION A silver-blue Chinese jian weapon design with icy white steel cutting edges, short dark-blue grips, tiny gold crossguards and restrained electric blue streaks. Preserve both actors, their exact outfits and ground positions, the single sword held in the Wudang hero's hand pointing right, the dark-robed target and the same silver-blue marker centered on the target's feet, warm neutral stone paving, fixed elevated orthographic camera, scale, 2x2 panels and existing numbers 1, 2, 3, 4. Change the timing and visibility of only the spectral swords and their effects to a four-beat story: aim, launch high, a clear empty pause, delayed dive onto the one target. No connecting arc or trail from caster to target should remain visible. Use separate readable effects instead of text or arrows. Do not add any text other than the original numbers.

1 TOP LEFT. Preserve the pointing cast pose and the small silver-blue mark under the boss's feet. Clear sky/air above both characters.
2 TOP RIGHT. A dense stream of more than a dozen visible blades leaves from directly behind the hero's rear shoulder and shoots nearly straight UP in a narrow column, like fireworks lifting off. UPWARD jian orientation: the pointed steel tip at the top, gold crossguard and dark blue grip at the lower end. As the first few swords reach the very high edge of the frame, they break into faint blue silver motes and vanish. The launch remains wholly over the hero's back at screen left; the space above the boss at right is empty.
3 BOTTOM LEFT. A conspicuous quiet beat immediately after the launch. Entire air completely EMPTY across the entire panel. Absolutely zero spectral swords, trails, arc, portal, particle stream or sky glow. The only change from the first panel is a slightly more luminous tight marker pulsing at the target's feet, telegraphing the delay. The hero still holds the one real sword. The exact same boss remains standing inside the mark. The absence of any sky VFX is critical.
4 BOTTOM RIGHT. One striking new volley materializes from offscreen at the top, directly over the single marked boss, and plunges straight down into the same ground point. DOWNWARD jian orientation is mandatory and unmistakable: at the top of each sword is the dark blue handle/pommel, directly below it the short GOLD CROSSGUARD, and the long SILVER blade and acute TRIANGULAR POINT extend DOWN below the guard toward the stone floor. Show many complete small swords pointing down like hanging icicles, with vertical blue trails ABOVE their handles. A few tips just reach the small impact splash right at the boss's feet. No angled flight across the middle of the screen, no launch effects or air swords near the hero, no broad carpet of impacts. Keep the boss body and all held weapons legible. Match the original reference image's sharp, carefully drawn wuxia pixel art without blur.

options.name: A1 · Bạch Phong
options.prompt:
Create a single original gameplay ART DIRECTION STORYBOARD for Võ Lâm Hero Defense, not a production sprite sheet. Use the references only as design inputs. Reference 1 is the accepted Wudang sword hero identity: exact compact chibi proportions, black high topknot, white trailing hair ribbons, black-charcoal vest over layered ivory sleeves and robe, black boots, ONE straight slim silver Chinese jian with a small brass guard in the right hand. Reference 2 defines the school's pixel-art costume and white/pale-blue sword-energy language. Reference 3 defines the actual fixed elevated orthographic three-quarter Pokémon-like camera, stone court and sprite scale. Read clearly as a game effect: hand-finished high-detail wuxia pixel art, crisp coherent outlines, clean opaque cel shapes, actual steel blade visible in hand, no motion blur smeared across the hero, each silhouette fully in frame. Keep the actor and ground contact consistent across panels. Background restrained warm gray-beige stone practice court per frame with muted contrast so white and dark energy both read; no architecture, no UI, no healthbars, no watermark, no fancy borders, no distracting text. Thin dark slate gutters and small simple numerals in the upper left are allowed. Spacious landscape storyboard with distinct non-overlapping panels.
Storyboard for FIVE independent normal attack variants of the exact SAME hero. The shared target direction is toward the RIGHT of the screen at a slight downward angle. Lay out a regular 3-column by 2-row grid of equal square-ish panels. Top row reads 1,2,3 and bottom row reads 4,5, PROC. Each of first five panels is a full-body contact key pose at matching scale and feet pivot, with a narrow movement trail revealing exactly how the sword moved. 1 = STRAIGHT THRUST: crouched lunge with front knee bent, right arm fully extended forward, jian horizontal with a perfectly straight thin thrust streak. 2 = LEFT CUT: backhand horizontal sweep across the front toward the hero's left, blade ends across the left side, crossed torso and leading forearm. 3 = RIGHT CUT: opposite forehand horizontal sweep across the front toward the hero's right, uncrossed open torso, blade exits outward, distinct reversed trail. Both horizontal cut poses still face their target at screen right; do not mirror whole actor to point left. 4 = DOWN CUT: visible overhead origin above the head, blade travels DOWN to the ground in front, low ending hand, bright top-to-bottom diagonal trace, weight forward. 5 = UP CUT: sword starts by front ankle and RISES diagonally to shoulder height and beyond, hands and blade end visibly HIGH, weight lifts, reversed vertical curve and tip glint at the high end. No duplicates or combined moves. Sixth panel PROC = visual reference only, one optional existing slim icy blue-white blade of sword qi detaches from the weapon tip and streaks forward to the right, no extra input or combo step. Reference 4 is the existing sword-qi shape to retain.
Art option BACH PHONG: precise and economical martial body mechanics, slender bright silver contact traces with cool ice-blue edge sparkle, tiny dust under feet. Each cut has one sharp, clean luminous edge and plenty of empty space. Main emphasis is instantly readable five different sword directions. PROC retains the existing cool-blue pointed sword-qi silhouette.
